I’m with the group on the π part and I think that’s settled. With per-haplotype deletion probability q>0 and reference imputation,
E[f_obs|f]=(1-q)f, so H_obs=2f_obs(1-f_obs)=2(1-q)f[1-(1-q)f]<2f(1-f)=H_true.
A true derived-reference pairwise comparison is scored as a match whenever the derived copy is the one that is filtered and put back to reference, so on the VCF-ascertained panel
E[hat π_obs]=L^{-1}∑E[2f_s,obs(1-f_s,obs)]<L^{-1}∑2f_s(1-f_s)=π_true
and the f→(1-q)f attenuation is O(1) in n. That downward frequency-weighted bias persists for every n.

Post-imputation a truly segregating ascertained site with K=k>0 true derived copies is seen as monomorphic reference iff all k carriers are filtered in their own samples.

Pr{K_obs=0|K=k}=q^k>0, Pr{site stays segregating|k}=1-q^k.

E[S_obs]=∑_s E[1-q^{K_s}]=θ∑_{i=1}^{2n-1}(1-q^i)/i
       =θ a_{2n-1}-θ∑_{i≥1}q^i/i
and
E[hat θ_W,obs]=θ[∑_i(1-q^i)/i]/a_{2n-1}=θ[1-∑_i q^i/i /a_{2n-1}]<θ
for every finite n as soon as q>0. ∑_i q^i/i=-log(1-q)>0 is the expected absolute loss of segregating sites turned to apparent fixed reference by the all-carriers-deleted event.

The problem asks about the resulting calculation from the imputed alignment that is actually fed to the estimators, on an arbitrarily large but finite sample with a substantial minority q>0 filtered and imputed to reference. For any realizable n, E[S_obs]<S_true strictly, so E[hat θ_W,obs]<θ strictly; the bias is O(1)/log n relative and vanishes only in the mathematical limit n→∞.

Thus on the data actually used both statistics are systematically underestimated relative to the true values on the ascertained SNV panel: π by the (1-q) frequency attenuation, and θ_W=S_obs/a_n by the 1-q^k loss of segregating sites. That is the both-downward case.

The per-haplotype step is an independent deletion of a true derived call with
per haplotype probability $q>0$ followed by reference imputation.

A true reference chromosome is always seen as reference and a true derived
chromosome is seen as derived with probability $1-q$ and as reference with
probability $q$.  On the VCF ascertained panel $f_{s}>0$

${\rm E}[f_{s}^{obs}\mid f_{s}]=(1-q)f_{s}$,

$H_{s}^{obs}=2f_{s}^{obs}(1-f_{s}^{obs})
        =2(1-q)f_{s}\big[1-(1-q)f_{s}\big]<2f_{s}(1-f_{s})=H_{s}^{true}$,

so a true derived-reference pairwise comparison is scored as a match
whenever the derived copy is the one that is filtered and imputed to
reference.  With $L$ ascertained sites

${\rm E}[\hat\pi_{obs}]
 =L^{-1}\sum_{s}{\rm E}\!\left[2f_{s}^{obs}(1-f_{s}^{obs})\right]
 <L^{-1}\sum_{s}2f_{s}(1-f_{s})=\pi_{true}$,

essentially ${\rm E}[\hat\pi_{obs}]\approx(1-q)\pi_{true}$ on the rare-site
dominant human spectrum.  The $f\mapsto(1-q)f$ attenuation is $O(1)$ in $n$
and does not vanish as $n\to\infty$.  Nucleotide diversity is frequency
weighted and is systematically depressed by reference imputation for every
$n$.

Presence/absence is different.  Conditional on $K_{n}=k>0$ true derived
copies in $2n$ haplotypes

${\rm Pr}\{K_{n}^{obs}=0\mid k\}=q^{k},\qquad
{\rm Pr}\{{\rm site\;seen\;segregating}\mid k\}=1-q^{k}$,

so on the SNV-ascertained panel

${\rm E}[S_{obs}]
 =\sum_{k\ge1}{\rm E}[S_{k}][1-q^{k}]
 =\theta\sum_{i=1}^{2n-1}\frac{1-q^{i}}{i}
 =\theta a_{2n-1}-\theta\sum_{i\ge1}\frac{q^{i}}{i}$,

${\rm E}[\hat\theta_{W,obs}]
 =\theta\frac{\sum_{i}(1-q^{i})/i}{a_{2n-1}}
 =\theta\Bigl[1-\frac{\sum_{i}q^{i}/i}{a_{2n-1}}\Bigr]
 =\theta\Bigl[1-\frac{-\log(1-q)+o(1)}{a_{2n-1}}\Bigr]$.

$\sum_{i}q^{i}/i=-\log(1-q)<\infty=O(1)$ whereas $a_{2n-1}\sim\log n\to\infty$.
For any fixed $f>0$, $K_{n}=2nf\to\infty$ and $q^{K_{n}}\to0$, so
${\rm Pr}\{K_{n}^{obs}>0\mid f>0\}\to1$.  The absolute expected loss of
ascertained segregating sites is $\theta\sum q^{i}/i=O(1)$ whereas
$S_{true}\sim\theta a_{n}\to\infty$, hence

${\rm E}[\hat\theta_{W,obs}]/\theta\to1,\qquad
S_{obs}=S_{true}+o_{p}(S_{true}),$

on the ascertained SNV panel.  The indicator ${\bf1}\{S_{i}>0\}$ on which
Watterson's estimator is based is asymptotically preserved by the random
independent deletion plus reference imputation; the $O(1)$ loss of the very
rarest copies is $o(a_{n})$ relative to $S$.

The usual upward SNV-only ascertainment bias is common to both estimators
with respect to a genome-wide $\theta$.  Differentially with respect to the
true values on the ascertained panel, the filter + reference imputation
step gives a first-order frequency dependent downward bias of $\pi$ while
$\hat\theta_{W}=S_{obs}/a_{n}$ is asymptotically robust in the

Strictly for any finite $n$ we have ${\rm E}[S_{obs}]<S_{true}$ and

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The per-haplotype mechanism is now settled across all colleagues. Deletion of a true derived call with per-haplotype probability q>0 followed by reference imputation gives a true reference always reference, a true derived seen derived with prob 1-q and imputed reference with prob q. Hence E[f_obs|f]=(1-q)f and H_obs=2f_obs(1-f_obs)=2(1-q)f[1-(1-q)f] <2f(1-f)=H_true. For rare sites H_obs≈(1-q)H_true. A true derived–reference pairwise comparison is scored as a match whenever the derived copy is filtered. So E[π_obs]=L^{-1}∑E[2f_obs(1-f_obs)] < π_true, with attenuation (1-q) O(1) in n and does not vanish as n→∞. Pi is frequency weighted and is systematically depressed by reference imputation for every n.

Watterson is presence/absence. Conditional on true derived count K=k>0, Pr[K_obs=0|k]=q^k, Pr{site seen segregating}=1-q^k. On the SNV-ascertained panel E[S_obs]=∑_s E[1-q^{K_s}]=θ∑_{i=1}^{2n-1}(1-q^i)/i = θ a_{2n-1} - θ∑ q^i/i. ∑ q^i/i = -log(1-q)<∞=O(1) whereas a_n∼log n→∞. For any fixed f>0, K_n=2nf→∞ and q^{K_n}→0, so Pr{site stays segregating|f>0}→1. The expected absolute loss of ascertained segregating sites is θ∑ q^i/i = -θlog(1-q)>0, O(1), while S_true∼θ a_n→∞. Hence E[θ̂_W,obs]/θ→1, S_obs=S_true+o_p(S_true) on the ascertained SNV panel in the n→∞ limit. The indicator 1{S_i>0} is asymptotically preserved; Watterson is frequency-blind to the (1-q) attenuation.

Finite-n vs asymptotic limit is the split. Colleagues 1,2,3,5 give the asymptotic statement: on the ascertained variant-only panel π is first-order downward biased by reference imputation, θ_W is asymptotically robust, relative bias O(1)/log n →0, i.e. answer B up to the common SNV-only ascertainment. Colleagues 4,6,7 stress that for any finite n, q^k>0 for every k, so E[S_obs]<S_true strictly and E[θ̂_W,obs]=θ[1-∑ q^i/i /a_n]<θ. The loss is concentrated in the rare tail, singletons lost with prob q, doubletons q^2, etc., and under infinite sites k=O(1) variants are continually replenished as n grows. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ is pre-filter ascertainment; post-imputation a truly segregating ascertained site can become monomorphic reference when all its carriers are filtered. Hence both statistics are systematically underestimated relative to the true values on the ascertained panel for any realizable sample, i.e. answer C.

The remaining tension is interpretation of “number of samples is arbitrarily large”. If taken as mathematical limit n→∞, relative bias of θ_W vanishes and differential bias introduced by filter+reference imputation is π-only downward, B. If taken as large but finite, O(1) loss ∑q^i/i gives a strictly positive finite-sample downward bias to both θ_W and π, C. Shared upward SNV-only ascertainment bias affects both estimators equally and is not the differential bias in question. The classic S vs H distinction is preserved: π is systematically biased down by reference imputation, θ_W is asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained panel, with strict finite-n downward bias O(1)/log n.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: Data generation is per-haplotype independent censoring of true derived calls with per-haplotype deletion probability q>0 and reference imputation of the deleted copies. True reference is always seen as reference, true derived is seen as derived with prob 1-q and as reference with prob q. On the SNV-ascertained panel f_s>0.

E[f_obs|f]=(1-q)f
H_obs=2f_obs(1-f_obs)=2(1-q)f[1-(1-q)f] <2f(1-f)=H_true
so a true derived–reference pairwise comparison is scored as a match whenever the derived copy is filtered. Hence
E[π̂_obs]=L^{-1}∑E[2f_obs(1-f_obs)] < π_true
≈(1-q)π_true for f≪1
The f→(1-q)f attenuation is O(1) in n and does not vanish as n→∞. Nucleotide diversity is frequency-weighted and is systematically depressed by reference imputation for every n. This is undisputed across colleagues.

Watterson is presence/absence. Conditional on K_n=k>0 true derived copies
Pr[K_obs=0|k]=q^k, Pr[site seen segregating|k]=1-q^k
On the ascertained SNV panel E[S_k]=θ/k so
E[S_obs]=θ∑_{i=1}^{2n-1}(1-q^i)/i =θ a_{2n-1}-θ∑_{i≥1}q^i/i
E[θ̂_W,obs]=θ[1-∑q^i/i /a_{2n-1}]
         =θ[1+log(1-q)/a_{2n-1}+o(1/a_n)].
∑ q^i/i = -log(1-q)=O(1) while a_{2n-1}∼log n→∞. For any fixed f>0, K_n=2nf→∞ and q^{K_n}→0, so Pr[site lost|f>0]→0. The absolute expected loss of segregating sites is θ[-log(1-q)]=O(1) whereas S_true∼θ a_n→∞. Hence
S_obs=S_true+o_p(S_true), E[θ̂_W,obs]/θ→1, n→∞
on the SNV-ascertained set. The indicator 1{S_i>0} on which Watterson is based is asymptotically preserved; the O(1) loss is o(a_n) relative.

The shared SNV-only ascertainment inflates both estimators w.r.t. a genome-wide θ, but the differential bias introduced by delete+reference imputation is a first-order downward frequency-dependent bias of π only in the n→∞ regime. This is the classic S vs H distinction and the basis for the B position argued by colleagues 1,2,3,5.

Finite-n strict inequality remains: for any finite n and q>0, 1-q^k<1 so E[S_obs]<S_true and E[θ̂_W,obs]=θ[1-∑q^i/i /a_n]<θ strictly. The loss is concentrated in the rare tail: singletons lost with prob q, doubletons q^2, etc. Under infinite sites the k=O(1) tail is continuously replenished as n grows, giving perpetual positive absolute loss. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ is a pre-filter ascertainment statement; post-imputation a truly segregating ascertained site can become monomorphic reference. This is the basis for the C position argued by colleagues 4,6,7.

Hinge remains interpretation of “number of samples is arbitrarily large”. Under the stated infinite-sample limit the relative bias of θ̂_W is o(1) and vanishes, leaving pi-only differential bias, i.e. B on the ascertained panel. Under a strict finite-sample interpretation E[θ̂_W,obs]<θ for any q>0, so both π and θ_W are downward biased relative to the true values on the ascertained panel, i.e. C. Current leaning stays with the asymptotic reading used by 1,2,3,5: π systematically downward biased, θ_W asymptotically robust on the ascertained SNV panel, with the finite-n O(1)/a_n downward loss of θ_W acknowledged as real and the source of the disagreement.

reflection_text.5:
Data generation is per-haplotype independent censoring of true derived calls with per-haplotype deletion probability q>0 and reference imputation of the deleted copies. True reference is always seen as reference, true derived is seen as derived with prob 1-q and as reference with prob q. On the SNV-ascertained panel f_s>0.

E[f_obs|f]=(1-q)f
H_obs=2f_obs(1-f_obs)=2(1-q)f[1-(1-q)f] <2f(1-f)=H_true
so a true derived–reference pairwise comparison is scored as a match whenever the derived copy is filtered. Hence
E[π̂_obs]=L^{-1}∑E[2f_obs(1-f_obs)] < π_true
≈(1-q)π_true for f≪1
The f→(1-q)f attenuation is O(1) in n and does not vanish as n→∞. Nucleotide diversity is frequency-weighted and is systematically depressed by reference imputation for every n. This is undisputed across colleagues.

Watterson is presence/absence. Conditional on K_n=k>0 true derived copies
Pr[K_obs=0|k]=q^k, Pr[site seen segregating|k]=1-q^k
On the ascertained SNV panel E[S_k]=θ/k so
E[S_obs]=θ∑_{i=1}^{2n-1}(1-q^i)/i =θ a_{2n-1}-θ∑_{i≥1}q^i/i
E[θ̂_W,obs]=θ[1-∑q^i/i /a_{2n-1}]
         =θ[1+log(1-q)/a_{2n-1}+o(1/a_n)].
∑ q^i/i = -log(1-q)=O(1) while a_{2n-1}∼log n→∞. For any fixed f>0, K_n=2nf→∞ and q^{K_n}→0, so Pr[site lost|f>0]→0. The absolute expected loss of segregating sites is θ[-log(1-q)]=O(1) whereas S_true∼θ a_n→∞. Hence
S_obs=S_true+o_p(S_true), E[θ̂_W,obs]/θ→1, n→∞
on the SNV-ascertained set. The indicator 1{S_i>0} on which Watterson is based is asymptotically preserved; the O(1) loss is o(a_n) relative.

The shared SNV-only ascertainment inflates both estimators w.r.t. a genome-wide θ, but the differential bias introduced by delete+reference imputation is a first-order downward frequency-dependent bias of π only in the n→∞ regime. This is the classic S vs H distinction and the basis for the B position argued by colleagues 1,2,3,5.

Finite-n strict inequality remains: for any finite n and q>0, 1-q^k<1 so E[S_obs]<S_true and E[θ̂_W,obs]=θ[1-∑q^i/i /a_n]<θ strictly. The loss is concentrated in the rare tail: singletons lost with prob q, doubletons q^2, etc. Under infinite sites the k=O(1) tail is continuously replenished as n grows, giving perpetual positive absolute loss. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ is a pre-filter ascertainment statement; post-imputation a truly segregating ascertained site can become monomorphic reference. This is the basis for the C position argued by colleagues 4,6,7.

Hinge remains interpretation of “number of samples is arbitrarily large”. Under the stated infinite-sample limit the relative bias of θ̂_W is o(1) and vanishes, leaving pi-only differential bias, i.e. B on the ascertained panel. Under a strict finite-sample interpretation E[θ̂_W,obs]<θ for any q>0, so both π and θ_W are downward biased relative to the true values on the ascertained panel, i.e. C. Current leaning stays with the asymptotic reading used by 1,2,3,5: π systematically downward biased, θ_W asymptotically robust on the ascertained SNV panel, with the finite-n O(1)/a_n downward loss of θ_W acknowledged as real and the source of the disagreement.
